newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on buying in blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on buying in blue-chips.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Wednesday on buying in blue-chips, but trading volume was thin with institutions sidelined due to market uncertainties before the issue of 1996 company results, brokers said.
All firms are required to issue 1996 results before April 30.
The B index inched up 0.435 points or 0.66 percent to 66.731 points on volume of 14.68 million shares worth $7.03 million, down from $8.39 million on Tuesday.
"Individual buying in counters expected to post good 1996 results pushed the index up," said one broker.
Another broker said institutional investors had little interest in building positions due to uncertainty over firms' results.
Brokers said they expected the index to meet resistance at 68 points in the near future.
A total of 43 B shares traded, with 23 up, 12 flat and eight down.
Building material maker Shanghai Huili was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.012 or 4.76 percent to $0.264 on volume of 179,000 shares.
Blue-chip Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor traded the most on anticipation of good 1996 results, gaining $0.024 or 4.49 percent to $0.558 on volume of 2.1 million shares.
Shanghai A shares rose on selective institutional buying, with a cautious mood dominating the market, brokers said.
The index closed up 14.374 points or 1.35 percent to 1,78.204 points on volume of 573.7 million shares worth 5.9 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index rose 14.374 points or 1.35 percent to 2,811.623 points.
Clothing maker Kangsai was the star on the release of good annual results, jumping 2.13 yuan or 10.00 percent to 23.43 yuan on volume of 700,100 shares.
